rows.grounds: accusative object identifying the syllable ca; bīja/mantra element transliterated by function
compound adjective qualifying chakāraṃ; expresses the wondrous nature of the syllable
indeclinable emphasizing self-identity of the subject
compound noun naming the goddess as the supreme kuṇḍalī, subject of the identification

items.question: What wondrous identity does the supreme kuṇḍalī embody in the form of the ca-syllable?
premises: The supreme kuṇḍalī is identified with the ca-syllable.
The ca-syllable is characterized as a supreme wonder.
This identification is affirmed as her own intrinsic nature.
items.inference: Therefore the ca-syllable is the supreme kuṇḍalī's own wondrous self-manifestation.
uncertainties: The implicit predicate linking chakāraṃ and parama+kuṇḍalī is supplied from context.
items.plain_english: The supreme kuṇḍalī is herself the ca-syllable, a supreme wonder.
